# Document template specs: the grammar

## Contents

- The spec
- Fields (`fields.<key>`)
- Blocks (`body`)
- Rules (`if`)
- Signer fields (`[[kind:Role:Label]]`)
- Salesforce fields and tables (Word format)
- Bulk send (`bulkSend`)
- Not supported, and why
- Add to Envelope Template
- Limits left as warnings (not enforced)

How to write a spec in `assets/document-templates/specs/` (or a lab spec) that `buildDocumentTemplate()`
(`src/document-template-spec.ts`) compiles into a template Create New imports. The import format, the ADF
body and the evidence behind each rule are in [DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES-CONFIG.md](DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES-CONFIG.md).
The library's specs are GENERATED (`captures/document-template-library.ts`); edit the generator, not a spec.
CI's `npm run doclib:check` fails when a committed spec differs from the generator's output.

Two formats share one grammar. **builder** (the default) is the Agreement Template Builder's format (ADF v1).
**word** (`"format": "word"`) is the Word/Template Assistant format (ADF v2), the only one with formulas.
"Proved" below means generated live on the legacy account (a verify report or a CFG note); everything else
compiles but has not been run.

## The spec

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | File name and verify-report name. Lab specs start `zz-`. |
| `name` | yes | The template's name. 1–100 characters (Create New's name box, `gallery/text/templates/01a-template-create-upload.txt`). The verifier prefixes `ZZ Lab · ` (9 more characters). |
| `description` | no | Documentation only; never compiled. |
| `agreementType` | no | The platform type's name (`Msa`, `Nda`, `OrderForm`…). Checked against the platform list: the Agreement Type enum the Workflow Builder shows (`NAVIGATOR_PROPS` in `src/workflow-navigator.ts`, harvested 2026-10-23); an unknown name is refused. Default `Other`, which that enum labels "Miscellaneous", the documented default (https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=map332c3ebc-8fca-4fac-9b9f-c7206adc3985&topicId=tskb006a75f-cb87-4d43-b47d-704e2d03f476.html&_LANG=enus). |
| `format` | no | `builder` (default) or `word`. |
| `header`, `footer` | no | Word format only: text printed at the top and bottom of every page; `{page}` and `{pages}` print the page number and the page count (`"Confidential · Page {page} of {pages}"`). Plain text, no field merges. Stored as the template's Word file stores them (`word/header1.xml`, `word/footer1.xml`), the shape a Word upload has (harvest 2026-10-31). Proved: library `purchase-agreement` generated with both ([verify](../assets/document-templates/verify/purchase-agreement.json)). The builder format has no header or footer and refuses them. |
| `fields` | yes | Sender fields, by key (below). Every declared field must be used. |
| `signers` | yes | Role names, in order, at least one, no repeats. Every role is "Needs to Sign" — the only recipient type a document template takes. A document template has **no signing order**: the builder's Edit Recipients holds role names only (lab 2026-10-30), so `routingOrder` is refused; the order is set in the workflow's Send step or an eSignature template. |
| `body` | yes | Blocks (below). |
| `bulkSend` | no | `true`: the compile also writes the bulk send list (`documentTemplateBulkCsv`; a bundle carries it as `NN-document-template-<id>.bulk-send.csv`). Below. |
| `examples` | for verify; a solution needs ≥1 | One Use Template run each: `values` (key → typed text), `tables` (line-item table name → CSV rows), `expect` / `absent` (strings the generated PDF must / must not contain). A number value takes at most 2 decimals. Every line-item table needs rows in every example, even one inside a rule. |

## Fields (`fields.<key>`)

A key is letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter. A field is printed with `{{key}}` in any text.

| Attribute | Meaning | Proved |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | What Use Template shows. A provision-bound field shows Docusign's label instead. | yes |
| `type` | `text` (default), `number`, `date`, `select`. | all four |
| `required` | `true` makes it required on the form. | form only |
| `description` | Help text under the label (a provision shows Docusign's). | no (not compared) |
| `options` | `select` only: the choices, in order, no repeats. | yes |
| `optionValues` | `select` only: option → what the document PRINTS (Use Template lists the option, the PDF prints the value). Keys must be options. A value that is a minted key (`Fontara_Inc`, so a workflow can fill the field from a request dropdown) is refused when the body prints `{{field}}`: print the text with one rule per option instead. | yes |
| `dateFormat` | `date` (builder proved; Word format written the same way and used for the Salesforce order forms' dates — compiled, not separately proved): `MM/dd/yyyy`, `dd/MM/yyyy` or `yyyy/MM/dd` — how the field prints and how Use Template's date box reads it (stored twice: the data field's `format.date.dateFormatPattern` and the form field's `format: { expression: <pattern>, locale }` — both are needed). | yes (lab specs `zz-dt-date-mdy/-dmy/-ymd`, 2026-10-25) |
| `numberFormat` | builder `number` only: `1,234.56` (en-US, the DEFAULT for a non-money, non-Salesforce number since 2026-10-29: with no format a workflow's Prepare Document Template printed 12 as "12/01/2001", while eSignature generation printed 12) or `1.234,56` (de-DE) — the editor's two formats besides none; grouping, up to 2 decimals. Stored as the data field's `format.number` and the form field's `{ expression: '#,##0.##', locale }`. **The sender types in the field's notation**: a `1.234,56` field read `1234567.5` as 12.345.675. No format prints the number as typed. | `1,234.56`: yes (`zz-dt-number-en`); `1.234,56`: yes (`zz-dt-number-de`: typed `1234567,5`, printed `1.234.567,5`) |
| `money` | `number` only: prints `1,440,000.00`. The number format of the builder's Currency type, without its account-wide custom field. | yes |
| `formula` | Word format only: a JSONata expression over field keys and `Table.column` paths; not on the form. Write `$number(x)` (values arrive as text) and `$replace(x, ',', '')` for CSV amounts. A formula cannot be computed per table row. | yes |
| `bind` | Where the value is stored: `{ "provision": <name> }` or `{ "custom": <Name> }` (an existing account custom field `C_<Name>`; the library binds none). Omit for a field the template keeps to itself. | provisions: see below; custom: one probe |

**Provisions** (`DT_PROVISIONS`): `AgreementParty` (text), `EffectiveDate`, `ExpirationDate`, `ExecutionDate`
(dates), `Title`, `GoverningLaw`, `Jurisdiction`, `EmploymentLocation` (text), `HireDate`, `TerminationDate`
(dates). A bound field takes the provision's type. Proved: all ten (`Title` and `Jurisdiction` in both formats by `zz-dt-align-provisions` / `zz-dt-word-list-align`).

Six more, each proved alone on legacy 2026-10-25 (lab specs `zz-dt-prov-*`): `PaymentTerms`, `NdaType`,
`RenewalType`, `EmploymentType` (dropdowns with Docusign's own options; a spec may not list options for them),
`RenewalNoticeDate` (date) and `RenewalInfo` (text, Docusign's label "Additional Info"). **What prints differs**:
`PaymentTerms` prints the stored value (`THIRTY_DAYS`); the other three print the option's label (`Auto Renew`,
`Mutual`, `Full Time`).

Eight more, each proved alone on the lab account 2026-11-02 (B4-D1/D2, lab specs `zz-dt-prov-*`; paths from the
Agreement Manager record a workflow start carries): `Term` (Docusign's label "Initial Term Length"), `RenewalTerm`,
`RenewalNoticePeriod`, `RenewalExtensionPeriod`, `ConvenienceNoticePeriod`, `CauseNoticePeriod` (text: a period prints
what the sender typed, such as `60 days`; Agreement Manager keeps periods as ISO 8601 durations, `P60D`),
`LatePaymentFeePercent` and `PriceCapIncrease` (numbers). Library spec
[`key-terms-schedule`](../assets/document-templates/specs/key-terms-schedule.json) binds all eight.

**Refused by import on a second lab account** (400 `FieldNotFound`, "not supported in your current account", on
an Msa template, 2026-10-25): Total Contract Value (`financial/TotalValue`), Annual Contract Value (`financial/AnnualValue`)
and Limitation of Liability Cap (`financial/LiabilityCap/fixedAmount`). The help lists them as standard agreement fields. **Re-probed on the lab account (IAM), 2026-10-30: the same 400**
(lab `zz-dt-contract-values`), so they are an account limit, not a missing shape. Put a contract amount in a `number`
field with `money: true`. (One a second lab account template binds TotalValue —
made in the editor, perhaps under another type; not reproduced.)

## Blocks (`body`)

| Block | Extra keys | Builder | Word | Proved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{ "title": "…" }` | — | bold 16pt, centred | bold 16, centred | yes |
| `{ "h": "…" }` | — | bold 13pt paragraph | bold 12 paragraph | yes |
| `{ "p": "…" }` | `align`: `left` / `center` / `right` | paragraph | paragraph | yes, `align` too (both formats) |
| `{ "list": ["…"] }` | — | bulleted list | paragraphs starting `•` | yes, both formats |
| `{ "ol": ["…"] }` | — | numbered list (1. 2. 3.; listClass `ol-decimal-alpha-roman`) | List Number paragraphs on a list instance, as a Word upload stores them | builder: yes; Word: verify queued |
| `{ "h1" \| "h2" \| "h3": "…" }` | — | the model's heading nodes, styled by the template stylesheet | paragraphs with style HeadingN | builder: yes; Word: verify queued |
| `{ "pagebreak": true }` | — | page break node | a break node | builder: yes (the editor shows its divider); Word: verify queued |
| `{ "image": "assets/…/logo.png", "align"?: … }` | `align`: `left` / `center` / `right` | an `img` node, the file inline as a data URI (PNG/JPEG, < 1 MB) — harvested 2026-10-30 from Toolbar ▸ More ▸ Image | refused | yes (builder; `equipment-rental-agreement`) |
| `{ "table": { "header": [], "rows": [[]] } }` | builder only: `align` (one of left/center/right per column), `fill` (header row colour, `#fff2cc`), `borders: false` — what the editor's table popover offers (lab DT-H1, 2026-11-02; no column width or per-cell border) | static table, equal columns | same | yes; the formatting keys: verify queued |
| `{ "lineItems": { "name", "label", "columns": [{ "key", "label" }] } }` | — | Dynamic Table, rows from a CSV | loop row, rows from a CSV | yes |
| `{ "if": <condition or list>, "then": [blocks] }` | `match`: `any` (default) / `all`; builder only: `hide`, `else` | logic block | `<!-- if -->` rule, never nested (see Rules) | see Rules |
| `{ "sign": "<role>" }` | `title`, `company`, `email` (booleans) | Signature, Name, (Title, Company, Email), Date Signed | same | yes |

Any other key — a misspelt block or option — is an error. A table row must have as many cells as its header.
A line-item table name is letters and digits, unique; columns: 1–10 (builder), 1–20 (word), unique keys written like
field keys — letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter (the help bans `: # % ! ? @ ^ & * ( ) - + = [ ] { } ; / ,`
in table field names, [nhd1712957935412](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=als1679428547895&topicId=nhd1712957935412.html&_LANG=enus)). In the Word
format a column takes `"type": "money"`: a CSV's `1200.5` prints 1,200.50 (lab `zz-dt-word-table-money`; library
`statement-of-work`'s Hourly Rate, 2026-10-31). `"type": "number"` imports and generates; its print format is not checked. In the builder format column values are text: the builder's Create New Dynamic Table
takes column names only and a column opens no field panel (lab 2026-10-31), so a `type` there is refused — write
the CSV value formatted (`1,234.56`).

**Total row** (Word format): a number or money column takes `"total": true` or `"total": "Total:"` (the text printed
before the sum, as the product's Total row takes label text in the same cell, task-3893). The table gets one row after
its repeating row; that column's cell is a formula, `$sum(Table.$number(column))`, and a money column's total prints
1,234.56. Several columns may each have one. Compiled with the proved formula mechanism (a formula tag, as a sender
field's `formula`), NOT the product's own Total-row storage: how the template editor stores a Total row is not harvested,
so the builder format refuses `total`. [inferred] A formula tag in a table cell after the loop generates; not yet proved
live (library `quote-summary-salesforce`). Third-party table filters are not compiled.

**Inline text** (`title`, `h`, `p`, list items, table cells): `{{key}}` prints a field; `**bold**` (balanced
pairs, else an error); `[[kind:Role:Label]]` places a signer field. `*italic*` and `++underline++` (both formats; Word as a Word upload's run formats, harvest 2026-11-02) and `\n` (a line break, builder only) — builder proved rendered by `zz-dt-nodes` (2026-10-25).

## Rules (`if`)

A condition is `{ "field": <key>, <operator>: <value> }` with exactly one operator. A list of conditions is
combined by `match` (`any` = Apply any / `||`, `all` = Apply all / `&&`). A rule may hold any blocks,
including rules and line-item tables.

Builder format only (proved live, lab spec `zz-dt-rule-actions`, legacy 2026-10-25):
- `"hide": true` — the rule HIDES its blocks when the condition holds (stored `show: false`).
- `"else": [blocks]` — the Otherwise branch, shown when the condition does not hold (a second rule in the
  same logic block, `isDefault: true`, no conditions; the editor captions it "Otherwise").

The Word format compiles neither (the Template Assistant does offer "Hide content" — msu1680044506702 — but how v2
stores it is not harvested); write the opposite rule instead. The builder's operator enum, read from the
generator's own code (the `@ap/agreement-prep` bundle), is EqualTo, NotEqualTo, LessThan, LessThanEqualTo,
GreaterThan, GreaterThanEqualTo, IsTrue, IsFalse; groups are And / Or. "Contains", "Is empty" and a "None"
group belong to other Docusign widgets (workflow conditions, filters), not to document templates.
IsTrue / IsFalse have no sender field to test (there is no boolean sender type) and are not compiled.

| Operator | Builder | Word | Field types | Proved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `is` | `EqualTo` | `=` | any (a select's value must be an option) | yes |
| `isNot` | `NotEqualTo` | `!=` | any | yes, both formats |
| `gt` | `GreaterThan` | `>` | number | yes, both formats |
| `lt` | `LessThan` | `<` | number | yes, both formats |
| `gte` | `GreaterThanEqualTo` | `>=` | number | yes, both formats |
| `lte` | `LessThanEqualTo` | `<=` | number | yes, both formats |

A condition on a select with `optionValues` compares the stored VALUE (the compiler substitutes it). Text
comparisons ignore case in both formats (labs `zz-dt-word-case`, `zz-dt-builder-case`); the help's case-sensitive
note (ahh1679704095661) is about raw `{{ if }}` text in classic Word files, which the compilers do not write.

Proved live (lab specs `zz-rules-probe-builder` / `-word`, legacy 2026-10-24): in the builder format
`match: all` and `any`, a rule nested in a rule (outer false; outer true with inner true and false) and a
line-item table inside a rule all generate. In the Word format `match: any` and `isNot`/`lt`/`>=`/`<=` did;
**a rule nested in a rule FAILED whenever the outer rule was false** ("Merge Failed: … Missing parent node
for if_start or if_end node"). So the Word compiler never nests rules: an inner rule is written as a
sibling rule whose condition is the enclosing conditions AND its own, and the outer rule's content is split
around it. That flattening (outer false; outer and inner true; a rule nested in an `any` group), `match: all`
with `gt` true, and a line-item table inside a true rule were then proved in the Word format (lab spec
`zz-word-rules-narrow`, 5/5 examples, legacy 2026-10-24).

**Inline rules** (Word format): `[[if:field=value]]text[[/if]]` inside one paragraph's text shows the text only when the
field equals the value (the Template Assistant's inline rule, con1f1d1e0b). Lab `zz-dt-word-inline-rule` generated both
branches with the text kept in one paragraph (2026-10-28); library `statement-of-work` uses it. An `[[if:…]]` must close
in the same text. Text comparisons ignore case in BOTH formats: typed `mutual` matched `Mutual` (labs `zz-dt-word-case`, 2026-10-28, and
`zz-dt-builder-case`, the lab account 2026-11-02; reports in `assets/document-templates/live/`).

## Signer fields (`[[kind:Role:Label]]`)

`[[kind?:…]]` makes the field optional. A signer field inside a rule may be missing from a generated
document, so its tab is written `anchorIgnoreIfNotPresent: true` (both formats; Word format proved by lab
spec `zz-word-conditional-signer`, 2026-10-24).

| Kind | Envelope tab | In the editor | Proved |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initials:Role` | `initialHereTabs` | placed field | yes |
| `text:Role:Label` | `textTabs` | placed field | yes |
| `email:Role:Label` | `emailTabs` (an address the signer types) | shown as Text | yes |
| `company:Role` | `companyTabs` | placed field | yes |
| `attach:Role:Label` | `signerAttachmentTabs` | placed field | yes |
| `check:Role:Label` | `checkboxTabs` (builder: + a one-box `tabGroups` entry) | checkbox | yes |
| `radio:Role:Label:A\|B\|C` | `listTabs` (a dropdown; the builder has no radio) | dropdown | yes |
| `date:Role:Label` | `dateTabs` on hidden anchor text | not shown | yes (lab) |
| `approve:Role` / `decline:Role` | `approveTabs` / `declineTabs` | placed field | builder: yes (`zz-dt-approve-note`); Word: compiled the builder's way, not yet run (library `purchase-agreement`) |
| `note:Role:Text` | `noteTabs`, the text as its value | placed field | builder: yes (`zz-dt-approve-note`); Word: as approve |

**Signer-field properties** (both formats; checkbox groups builder only): a trailing segment `key=value;flag;…` —
`[[text:Customer:VAT number:tooltip=Your UK VAT number;width=240;max=11;pattern=^GB\d{9}$;message=GB and 9 digits]]`.

| Property | Tab property | Proved on the draft (`zz-dt-signer-props`, 2026-10-25) |
|---|---|---|
| `tooltip=…` | `tooltip` | yes (text and initials) |
| `width=N`, `max=N` | `width`, `maxLength` | yes |
| `pattern=…`, `message=…` | `validationPattern`, `validationMessage` | yes |
| `size=N`, `color=Name`, `bold` | `fontSize: sizeN`, `fontColor` (an eSignature colour name; stored lower-case), `bold` | yes |
| `conceal`, `locked` | `concealValueOnDocument`, `locked` | yes |

Without properties a field is Arial 11, width 180. A pattern cannot contain `]`.

**Checkbox groups**: `[[check:Role:Label:group=Contact;min=1;max=2]]`, then `[[check:Role:Other:group=Contact]]`
— boxes naming one group share it; min/max on the first give its rule (at least / at most / exactly / range).
Membership is proved (each draft checkbox's `tabGroupLabels`, `zz-dt-checkbox-groups`). **The rule is NOT
enforced in the generated envelope**: the template stores it, but generation does not carry it — the draft has
no `tabGroups` (both the recipients read and the per-recipient tabs read return none; every box reads back
`required: true`), legacy 2026-10-25. `min`/`max` still compile, for the template's own record.

**Links and styled runs** (builder): `[text](https://…)` is a link node; `[text]{color:#cc0000; font-size:18pt;
background-color:#ffff00; font-family:Georgia}` a styled run. Colour, size and highlight render (`zz-dt-styles`
screenshot, 2026-10-25). A `font-family` must be one of the editor's 23 menu fonts (Arial, Calibri, Cambria, Courier New,
Helvetica, Tahoma, Times New Roman, Verdana…; no Georgia, which is why Georgia did not render); it is stored as the editor
stores it, `times new roman, serif` (lab DT-H1, 2026-11-02). **A builder link is not kept by generation**: the template
stores the link node, but the generated PDF prints only its text, with no link annotation (library `engagement-letter`,
the lab account 2026-11-02, [report](../assets/document-templates/live/engagement-letter-link-2026-11-02.json)). Write the
URL in the text when the reader needs it. A Word-format link is kept (library `statement-of-work`, 2026-11-02).

## Salesforce fields and tables (Word format)

A spec that names a connection reads fields from the Salesforce record a workflow starts from:

```json
"format": "word",
"salesforce": { "connection": "default", "object": "Opportunity" },
"fields": { "customer": { "label": "Customer legal name", "salesforce": "SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r:SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Account__r:Account.Name" },
            "quote": { "label": "Quote number", "salesforce": "SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r:SBQQ__Quote__c.Name" } },
"body": [ { "lineItems": { "name": "OrderItems", "label": "Order items", "salesforce": "SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r:SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__LineItems__r:SBQQ__QuoteLine__c",
            "columns": [ { "key": "sku", "label": "SKU", "salesforce": "SBQQ__ProductCode__c" },
                         { "key": "net_amount", "label": "Total for the Term", "salesforce": "SBQQ__NetTotal__c", "type": "money" } ] } } ]
```

- `connection` names an entry of `SF_CONNECTIONS` (src/document-template-spec.ts): the account and its Salesforce
  connection. Only `default` is known: the lab account's connection (read from an editor-made template,
  e08cb251, 2026-10-27).
- `object` is the template's ROOT: the Salesforce record a workflow starts from and passes as `recordId`. Every
  path is relative to it, so one document read from two kinds of record is two templates (the library's
  `order-form-salesforce`, root Opportunity, and `order-form-salesforce-quote`, root `SBQQ__Quote__c`). A workflow's
  generate step must use a template whose root is its Salesforce start object.
- A field path starts at `object`; a relationship is its name when the target has the same name (`Account`),
  else `Name:Type`. A table is a child relationship `Relationship:Object`, or a chain through lookups
  joined by `.` (generation proved; the editor's Tables tab offers only DIRECT children of the source object, task-3893,
  so a lookup-chain table may not survive opening and saving the template in the editor — unprobed); every column names its field; `type: "number"` or `"money"` for a number or currency field
  (a currency is stored as an amount and a code; the column prints the amount, formatted 1,234.56).
- Formulas sum a Salesforce table like any other: `$sum(OrderItems.$number(net_amount))`. Values arrive as
  numbers, so there is no `$replace`.
- A picklist is a `select` whose `options` must be the org's active values. It can drive rules (proved: probe
  `zz-dt-sf-entity-picklist`, the lab account, 2026-10-28); it prints the picklist VALUE, so text an option used to print
  through `optionValues` comes from one rule per value instead (the Salesforce order forms' entity line). The compiler
  refuses Salesforce fields in the builder format: the product supports them there (tsk22feeaa4), but the builder's
  storage of them is not harvested. A date takes `dateFormat` (otherwise it prints ISO, 2026-11-08).
- Salesforce fields are optional by default: a REQUIRED connected field that comes back empty makes generation
  fill no Salesforce value at all (live, 2026-10-27), so the compiler warns when a spec makes one required.
- Stored as: a tag with `externalSource: "Salesforce"` and the path as `externalId`, NAMED after its path as the
  editor names it (`Opportunity_Account_28_Account_29_Name_<suffix>`); the form field's `fullyQualifiedPath`; the
  loop's `externalId`; the wrapper's `connectionDetails` (which import drops); fields and tables in ONE order,
  in document order.
- **Use Template cannot fill them.** A workflow's Prepare Document Template step generates them from the
  record. Such a template is created by `captures/document-template-create.ts` (the lab account, kept), and
  its generation is proved by a workflow run.

**Object-model versions** (deploy's report, 2026-10-27, the lab account):
- A path's namespace ends `@<n>`, the connection's object-model version. Both models exist: @1 (225 types) and
  @4 (305 types; the CPQ objects exist only at @4).
- **Docusign stores an imported template's paths at the connection's CURRENT version** (true, but not the
  cause of the empty Account fields; see below). A template compiled at
  @1 is stored at @4. Templates saved in the template editor keep the version they were bound at (e08cb251 is @1).
  So the compiler writes the current version (`SF_CONNECTIONS.default.version`, 6 since 2026-10-28), and there is no per-spec
  override: it would be rewritten at import.
- The version rewrite is NOT why a field came back empty. **A table read through a lookup empties every
  Salesforce field that follows a different relationship** (deploy,
  2026-10-27): `Opportunity/Account(:Account)/…` fills at @4 on its own, beside the quote's scalar fields, and
  beside a table read directly from the root (`OpportunityLineItems[]`). Add the quote's line items
  (`SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r(:SBQQ__Quote__c)/SBQQ__LineItems__r[]`) and the Account fields come back empty; with
  nothing else, populate answers 404 CdsNotFound. Fields on the root or through the same lookup still fill.
  **The compiler refuses** such a template and names the two fixes: read the field through the table's lookup
  (`SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r:SBQQ__Quote__c.SBQQ__Account__r:Account.Name`), or root the template at the lookup's
  object (`order-form-salesforce-quote`).
- **A Salesforce field must exist in the connection's object model, not only in the org.** Fields created in Salesforce
  after the model was last loaded (Account.Legal_Entity_Type__c, MSA_Date__c, Fontara_Entity__c on 2026-10-28) are absent from
  it, and a template bound to one fails at import: 404 `ERR_13009` "Failed to import workflow: Failed to create document
  template" (through a workflow package). Refresh the connection's objects in Docusign first; the refresh may bump the version
  (`SF_CONNECTIONS.default.version`), which the field search shows (`connected-data/v1/fields/search`). The 2026-10-28 refresh
  moved the lab account's connection from @4 to @6.0.0; @4 paths still resolve.
- Relationship names confirmed in the @4 model AND the org's describe: `SBQQ__PrimaryQuote__r`, `SBQQ__Account__r`,
  `SBQQ__LineItems__r` (the child relationship of `SBQQ__QuoteLine__c.SBQQ__Quote__c`), `OpportunityLineItems`,
  `Account`. All 26 paths the library binds resolve at @4.
- **Proved by generation** (deploy's test loop, 2026-10-27): `order-form-salesforce` (root Opportunity) and
  `order-form-salesforce-quote` (root `SBQQ__Quote__c`) fill all 13 Salesforce fields and tables.

## Bulk send (`bulkSend`)

Proved by the corpus spec [`legal-hold-notice-bulk`](../assets/prompt-corpus/expected/legal-hold-notice/document-templates/specs/legal-hold-notice-bulk.json)
on the lab account, 2026-10-31 ([live report](../assets/prompt-corpus/live/legal-hold-notice.json)): a list of two
zz-lab rows made two envelopes, and each generated document held its row's values. The columns (help
nan1681853631175, and the dialog's own sample list):

| Column | For |
|---|---|
| `<signer>::Name`, `<signer>::Email` | every signer role |
| `Document Generation::<label>` | each sender field, by its LABEL; every required one needs a value in every row |
| `Dynamic Table::<table label>\|<column label>` | each line-item column; the cell holds the table's rows split by `\|` (spaces kept) [inferred: by label like the fields; no table was in the proof] |

- **Labels, not names.** A list with the compiled names (`Document Generation::matter_id_socm98`) imports, but its
  preview reports every label column as missing and Save stays off. Two fields with one label would share a column:
  the compiler refuses that.
- The dialog's sample also lists `<signer>::Signature Provider`: optional (the import offers "Accept"), not written.
- **Where:** Use Template has NO bulk option. Start ▸ Envelopes ▸ Send Envelope ▸ Add documents ▸ Upload ▸
  **Document Templates** ▸ the template ▸ Add Selected; then Add recipients ▸ **Bulk send** ▸ Upload a file. The
  first screen's Sample File lists only the role columns; the matching-exceptions screen's "Download sample" lists
  the field labels.
- One example row: the spec's first example (a table's rows joined by `|`), `zz-lab.<role>-1@example.com` inboxes.
- Refused with `bulkSend`: more than 100 sender fields (a warning without it), a Salesforce connection (its fields
  fill from the record), a signer name with `( ) : ; < > @`.
- The help's limits: one document template per bulk send; same-named fields carry the same value.

## Not supported, and why

| Product feature | Why not |
|---|---|
| Currency type, new custom fields, shared (account) table definitions | Each creates a PERMANENT account-wide custom field in every importing account (CFG §7a, §7b). `money` and form-sourced tables do the same job. |
| Custom agreement types | The wrapper's FQN is the platform's (`platform.agreements@1.18.0`); a custom type's is unknown. |
| Builder-format Salesforce fields, other connections (HubSpot, a second lab account's Salesforce) | Not harvested: only the lab account's connection is known. |
| Other standard agreement fields (e.g. MSA's Annual Contract Value) | 16 provisions are known (above); TCV, ACV and the liability cap are refused by import on both accounts (400 FieldNotFound, re-probed on the lab account 2026-10-30); other paths are not harvested. |
| Number formats other than `money` in the Word format, default values (a Template Assistant feature, xou1680241342792), third-party table filters, the editor's own Total-row storage (`total` compiles a formula row instead) | Not harvested. |
| Headers/footers in the builder format (the builder has no control for them, lab 2026-10-30; a logo goes in as an `image` block; the Word format has `header`/`footer`), header/footer images and merged fields in a header; the Word format's italic/underline/numbered lists/headings/page breaks/links/styles | Not compiled (CFG §8). |
| Checkbox groups in the Word format | Not compiled. (Signer-field properties and Approve/Decline/Note compile in both formats.) |
| Classic `{{token}}` Word files, `SuppressParagraph` | Classic templates do not generate from Use Template (CFG §1). |

## Add to Envelope Template

`createEnvelopeTemplateViaApi` (`src/document-templates.ts`) makes an eSignature envelope template from a published
document template (`POST {dt}/document_templates/{id}/envelope_templates`, body `{}`; probe L-DT2). Facts from the
dialog (lab tpl-legacy, a second lab account 2026-11-02): a DOCX document template joins only envelope templates
whose documents are all DOCX, and later changes to the document template update the envelope template automatically.

## Limits left as warnings (not enforced)

- **Dropdown size and `;`** — the 250-option, no-semicolon limit is documented for the Template Assistant
  (dtw1680044374844) and now enforced in both formats (the builder's own limit is not documented).
- **A signer with no fields**, or a template with no `sign` block — compiles; INFERRED that sending may
  then refuse the envelope.
- **`gt`/`lt` on a date** is refused; compare dates with `is` / `isNot` only.
